title: Paid tax return preparers (IRS PTIN)
hypothesis: A PTIN row establishes a paid-preparer candidate and a published business phone, not an owner-confirmed person or direct owner handset. A surname-in-DBA row with a unique phone is a stronger owner and direct-line candidate; franchise, firm-employee, shared-office, and unresolved rows must not be represented as owner-confirmed.
ownerSource: IRS PTIN state extracts provide a preparer's name, DBA, business address, credential, and business phone. The implemented parser marks only whether the surname occurs in the DBA; it does not classify franchise employees, aggregate DBA/address firm size, select a firm principal, or confirm ownership.
phoneSource: BUS_PHNE_NBR is an explicitly published business phone, normalized by the IRS PTIN adapter. It is not mobile, reachable, DNC/TCPA-clear, exclusive, or owned by the named preparer. Reuse_count at most 3 is an implemented office-line screen, but does not prove a direct line.

workflow.label: IRS PTIN state extract
workflow.detail: Ingest the free public PTIN CSV: paid-preparer identity, DBA, business address, credential, AFSP flag, and published business phone.

workflow.label: Person and business-phone parse
workflow.detail: Keep person rows and normalize BUS_PHNE_NBR; hold malformed person or unusable phone rows.

workflow.label: PTIN input hold
workflow.detail: Hold non-person, missing-phone, toll-free, or otherwise unusable published-business-phone rows.

workflow.label: Owner-role assessment
workflow.detail: Keep surname-in-DBA or blank-DBA rows as owner candidates; reject known chain/franchise employee rows and hold non-surname firm rows pending a supported principal selection.

workflow.label: Employee or firm-role hold
workflow.detail: Hold franchise/national-chain staff, multi-preparer firm rows without a selected principal, and every row whose ownership remains unsupported.

workflow.label: Published phone reuse screen
workflow.detail: Require phone reuse_count at most 3; a reused number is an office-line candidate, never a named preparer's direct line.

workflow.label: Shared-office hold
workflow.detail: Hold phones reused by more than three register rows from direct-owner claims; preserve business-phone provenance only.

workflow.label: Maps contrast and bucket assignment
workflow.detail: For the adapter's recipe-D path, match the registered business to a relevant Maps listing and bucket register-only, differing-phone, or equal-phone cases. A differing line remains only a candidate.

workflow.label: Line and compliance gates
workflow.detail: Require mobile classification, reachability, DNC/TCPA clearance, suppression and duplicate checks, freshness, and timezone before delivery.

workflow.label: Phone or compliance hold
workflow.detail: Hold business/landline/VoIP, unreachable, DNC/TCPA, suppressed, duplicate, stale, or timezone-unresolved rows.

workflow.label: Owner and direct-contact proof
workflow.detail: Require supported ownership of the matched business and an explicit direct business-role link to the cleared phone; PTIN publication, DBA heuristic, credential, or line type alone is insufficient.

workflow.label: Ownership/contact proof hold
workflow.detail: Hold candidates with only a PTIN, surname heuristic, blank DBA, firm role, shared office phone, or unlinked business phone.

workflow.label: Future owner-confirmed delivery
workflow.detail: Deliver only after role, contact, compliance, and separate owner/direct-contact evidence all pass.

edges.label: employee, chain, firm, or unresolved role
phone reused more than three times

failures.risk: A PTIN holder, credential, or published business phone is represented as an owner-confirmed mobile.
failures.mitigation: Keep PTIN identity, business-phone provenance, ownership evidence, and handset/compliance evidence as separate gates.

failures.risk: H&R Block, other chains, or multi-preparer firm employees pass because the adapter only records dbaHasSurname.
failures.mitigation: Add an auditable chain/employee exclusion and a DBA-plus-address group rule; select a principal only with supported evidence, otherwise hold.

failures.risk: The live brain runs PTIN as recipe C although irsPtin and the catalog specify recipe D, so it bypasses Maps contrast and bucket evidence.
failures.mitigation: Align tax_preparer routing with the implemented irsPtin recipe D, or explicitly change the adapter/catalog semantics and add a regression test. Do not silently treat C verification as D evidence.

failures.risk: A phone reused by several PTIN rows is treated as a preparer's direct number.
failures.mitigation: Keep reuse_count greater than 3 out of direct-owner claims and retain it only as published office-phone evidence.

failures.risk: Blank DBA is converted from a weak sole-proprietor heuristic into owner proof.
failures.mitigation: Use blank DBA only to prioritize an owner candidate; require separate business ownership and direct-contact support.

iterations.hypothesis: The five-case saved PTIN fixture establishes a preparer identity and published business phone while correctly preserving only the DBA-surname heuristic.
iterations.test: Five-case local fixture/code audit on 2026-09-24: first five data rows of tests/fixtures/registers/irs_ptin.json through irsPtin. Command: node --experimental-strip-types --test --test-name-pattern='irs_ptin' tests/lead-engine-registers.test.ts. No network, paid provider, contact lookup, or private/residential data used.
iterations.observed: Five parsed person rows had normalized published business phones. Three DBA values contained the preparer surname (Kobert, Bantekas, Swett); H & R Block and Schreiner/Weskamp/Schmerge did not. The parser did not reject the chain row or classify employee versus firm principal. This is adapter evidence only, not an ownership, handset, reachability, DNC/TCPA, or delivery measurement.
iterations.change: Treat dbaHasSurname as an owner-candidate signal only; add role and firm/chain holds before an owner label, and align the brain route with the adapter's recipe-D contrast before relying on bucket evidence.

measurement.result: Five saved IRS PTIN fixture rows parsed: five person identities and five normalized published business phones; three surname-in-DBA candidates and two non-surname firm/chain rows. Fixture/code audit only; no live source, phone, owner, handset, compliance, or delivery measurement.

cost.basis: Local five-row fixture/code audit only; no source fetch, provider, append, trace, Maps scrape, or phone-verification call ran.
cost.note: No clean owner contact was measured. The brain's historical estimates use a different denominator and do not establish owner-contact cost.

implementation.summary: PTIN ingestion preserves a published-business-phone field, normalized format, surname-in-DBA flag, and phone reuse screen. It does not implement employee/franchise exclusion, firm-principal selection, owner confirmation, direct-owner-contact proof, or adapter/brain recipe alignment. The current recipe-C route can verify a registered business phone without the adapter's recipe-D Maps contrast.

nextMeasurement: After root aligns routing and adds an owner-role classifier, run a lawful 5–20 row aggregate sample only from the catalog-verified PTIN endpoint. Separate PTIN people, usable published business phones, chain/employee exclusions, firm-principal-supported candidates, reuse at most 3, bucket, mobile, reachable, DNC/TCPA-clear, owner-supported, direct-contact-supported, and delivered denominators; do not use residential/property sources, paid lookups, or prohibited lists.
